# student-citations-mcp

> Citation generator MCP server for APA, MLA and Chicago citations from a DOI or ISBN. No account. Version 0.1.5. Free and open source MCP server for AI apps (Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, Copilot and others).

## Setup
- Run with npx -y student-citations-mcp
- No key or account. Optional CROSSREF_EMAIL.
- Styles are apa7, mla9 and chicago-ad. format_citation and cite_from_doi also take all to return all three styles in one reply. Italics are returned as asterisks.
- All five tools are read only. Nothing is stored.
- The cite_this prompt looks nothing up. It only writes out the request.

## Tools

### format_citation
Format a journal article, book, website, book chapter, thesis, report, dataset or preprint as a citation in APA 7, MLA 9 or Chicago author date, from details you provide. Inputs: type (journal, book, website, chapter, thesis, report, dataset or preprint), title, and optional authors (family plus given names), year, container, publisher, city, edition, editors, translators, volume, issue, pages, doi, url, date_text, accessed, institution, degree, repository, report_number and style (apa7, mla9, chicago-ad or all). Pass all to get all three styles in one reply, each one with its style name on the line above it. Editors and translators are for books and take the same shape as authors: a book with editors and no authors puts the editors where the author goes, and a book with authors too carries the other names after the title, in the spot each style uses. Example prompt: "Cite this journal article in APA 7: Learning to learn by John Kenneth Smith and Alice Jones, 2020, Journal of Study Skills, volume 4, issue 2, pages 11-25."

Parameters:
- type (required): journal, book, website, chapter, thesis, report, dataset or preprint
- title (required): the title of the source
- authors (optional, default []): list of objects with family (last name) and given (first and middle names, optional), like [{"family": "Smith", "given": "John Kenneth"}]
- editors (optional): same shape as authors, for a book or a chapter. With no authors the editors go where the author goes, with the role word the style uses: Ed. or Eds. in APA, editor or editors in MLA, ed. or eds. in Chicago. With authors too they go after the title, inside the parentheses with the edition in APA and as "Edited by ..." in MLA and Chicago.
- translators (optional): same shape as authors, for a book. They go after the title, inside the parentheses as "Trans." in APA and as "Translated by ..." in MLA and Chicago.
- year (optional): publication year as text, like "2020"
- container (optional): Journal name, the book title for a chapter, or website name. Required for a journal article and for a chapter, since without it the citation would be missing the work it appears in.
- publisher (optional): publisher name
- city (optional): Publisher city, used by Chicago for books.
- edition (optional): For example "2nd".
- volume (optional): volume number as text, like "4"
- issue (optional): issue number as text, like "2"
- pages (optional): For example "11-25".
- doi (optional): a DOI for the source, printed as a doi.org link
- url (optional): a URL for the source
- date_text (optional): Website date as you want it shown, like "2026, October 14" for APA or "14 Oct. 2026" for MLA.
- accessed (optional): MLA access date, like "14 Oct. 2026".
- institution (optional): the university or organisation behind a thesis, a report or a dataset
- degree (optional): the degree of a thesis, like "Ph.D."
- repository (optional): where a preprint was posted, like arXiv
- report_number (optional): the number of a report or a standard
- style (optional, default apa7): Citation style. apa7, mla9 or chicago-ad (Chicago author date), or all to get all three in one reply with a label above each one.

Example: with type "journal", title "Learning to learn", authors [{"family": "Smith", "given": "John Kenneth"}, {"family": "Jones", "given": "Alice"}], year "2020", container "Journal of Study Skills", volume "4", issue "2", pages "11-25" and style "apa7", returns "Smith, J. K., & Jones, A. (2020). Learning to learn. *Journal of Study Skills*, *4*(2), 11-25."

All three styles: with the same details and style "all", returns the APA 7, MLA 9 and Chicago author date citations in that order, each one with its style name on the line above it, separated by blank lines.

Editors in the author's place: with type "book", title "A dictionary of study words", editors [{"family": "Patel", "given": "Jamie"}, {"family": "Cole", "given": "Robin"}], year "2019", publisher "North Gate Press" and style "mla9", returns "Patel, Jamie, and Robin Cole, editors. *A dictionary of study words*. North Gate Press, 2019.". The same book in apa7 returns "Patel, J., & Cole, R., Eds. (2019). *A dictionary of study words*. North Gate Press." and in chicago-ad returns "Patel, Jamie, and Robin Cole, eds. 2019. *A dictionary of study words*. North Gate Press."

Translators after the title: with type "book", title "My brilliant friend", authors [{"family": "Ferrante", "given": "Elena"}], translators [{"family": "Goldstein", "given": "Ann"}], year "2012", publisher "Europa Editions" and style "apa7", returns "Ferrante, E. (2012). *My brilliant friend* (Goldstein, A., Trans.). Europa Editions.".

### format_bibliography
Format several sources at once as one works cited list, alphabetised by the first author's family name, in APA 7, MLA 9 or Chicago author date. A source with no author is alphabetised by its title. Inputs: sources (an array of objects, each with the same fields as format_citation: type, title and optional authors, year, container, publisher, city, edition, editors, translators, volume, issue, pages, doi, url, date_text, accessed, institution, degree, repository and report_number) and style (apa7, mla9 or chicago-ad). Example prompt: "Put these three sources into an APA works cited list: a journal article by Smith and Jones from 2020, a book by Cormen from 2009 and a website from example.edu."

Parameters:
- sources (required): the sources for the list. Each one takes the same fields as format_citation: type (journal, book, website, chapter, thesis, report, dataset or preprint), title, and optional authors, year, container, publisher, city, edition, editors, translators, volume, issue, pages, doi, url, date_text, accessed, institution, degree, repository and report_number. A journal article, a book, a website, a chapter, a thesis, a report, a dataset and a preprint can share one list.
- style (optional, default apa7): Citation style. apa7, mla9 or chicago-ad (Chicago author date).

Example: with sources [{"type": "journal", "title": "Learning to learn", "authors": [{"family": "Smith", "given": "John Kenneth"}, {"family": "Jones", "given": "Alice"}], "year": "2020", "container": "Journal of Study Skills", "volume": "4", "issue": "2", "pages": "11-25"}, {"type": "book", "title": "Introduction to algorithms", "authors": [{"family": "Cormen", "given": "Thomas H."}], "year": "2009", "edition": "3rd", "publisher": "MIT Press"}, {"type": "website", "title": "The water cycle", "authors": [], "container": "Example Uni", "year": "2026", "url": "https://example.edu/water"}] and style "apa7", returns three entries separated by blank lines, in the order Cormen, Smith and the website, alphabetised by author and, for the website, by the title with "The" skipped.

### cite_from_doi
Look up a DOI on Crossref and format the citation. The Crossref record decides the shape: a journal article, a book or an edited book, a book chapter or a conference paper, a thesis, a report, a dataset or a preprint. Inputs: doi (a DOI like 10.1038/nature14539 or a doi.org link) and style (apa7, mla9, chicago-ad or all). Pass all to get all three styles in one reply, each one with its style name on the line above it. Example prompt: "Cite 10.1038/nature14539 in APA."

Parameters:
- doi (required): A DOI like 10.1038/nature14539, or a doi.org link.
- style (optional, default apa7): Citation style. apa7, mla9 or chicago-ad (Chicago author date), or all to get all three in one reply with a label above each one.

Example: with doi "10.1038/nature14539" and style "mla9", returns that DOI's Crossref record formatted in MLA 9, then a blank line and "(From Crossref. Check it against your style guide.)". If Crossref does not know the DOI, the tool returns an error message instead.

All three styles: with style "all", returns the APA 7, MLA 9 and Chicago author date citations in that order, each one with its style name on the line above it, then the same Crossref note.

How the Crossref type is read:
- Journal article: an article with its volume, issue and pages.
- Book, monograph, edited book, reference book, proceedings: a book, and the editors take the author's place when the book has no author.
- Book chapter, conference paper: a chapter in its book, with the pages it covers.
- Dissertation: a thesis, with the degree and the university.
- Report, standard: a report, with its report number.
- Dataset: a data set.
- Posted content: a preprint, with the repository it was posted in.

### cite_from_isbn
Look up an ISBN on Open Library and format the book citation. Inputs: isbn (a 10 or 13 digit ISBN, dashes are fine) and style (apa7, mla9 or chicago-ad). Example prompt: "Cite ISBN 978-0-262-03384-8 in MLA 9."

Parameters:
- isbn (required): A 10 or 13 digit ISBN. Dashes are fine.
- style (optional, default apa7): Citation style. apa7, mla9 or chicago-ad (Chicago author date).

Example: with isbn "978-0-262-03384-8" and style "mla9", returns that book's Open Library record formatted in MLA 9, then a blank line and "(From Open Library. Check it against your style guide.)". If Open Library has no book for the ISBN, the tool returns an error message instead.

### in_text_citation
The in text citation that goes with a source, with an optional page number and an optional narrative form for a sentence where the author is named. Give authors and year, or a doi or an isbn and the record fills them in. Inputs: authors (family name plus optional given names), year, doi, isbn, page, form (parenthetical or narrative) and style (apa7, mla9 or chicago-ad). A doi or an isbn cannot be combined with the other one. Example prompt: "Give the APA in text citation for Smith and Jones 2020 on page 14."

Parameters:
- authors (optional, default []): list of objects with family (last name) and given (first and middle names, optional), like [{"family": "Smith", "given": "John Kenneth"}]
- year (optional): publication year as text, like "2020"
- doi (optional): a DOI like 10.1038/nature14539 or a doi.org link. The lookup fills in the authors and the year.
- isbn (optional): a 10 or 13 digit ISBN, dashes are fine. The lookup fills in the authors and the year.
- page (optional): page number as text, like "14"
- form (optional, default parenthetical): parenthetical is the usual brackets, like (Smith & Jones, 2020, p. 14). narrative puts the author in your sentence and keeps the rest in brackets, like Smith and Jones (2020, p. 14).
- style (optional, default apa7): Citation style. apa7, mla9 or chicago-ad (Chicago author date).

Example: with authors [{"family": "Smith", "given": "John Kenneth"}, {"family": "Jones", "given": "Alice"}], year "2020" and page "14", style "apa7" returns "(Smith & Jones, 2020, p. 14)", style "mla9" returns "(Smith and Jones 14)" and style "chicago-ad" returns "(Smith and Jones 2020, 14)".

With doi "10.1038/nature14539" and page "436", style "apa7" returns "(LeCun et al., 2015, p. 436)" from the Crossref record, and style "mla9" returns "(LeCun et al. 436)". With isbn "978-0-262-03384-8", style "apa7" returns "(Cormen & Leiserson, 2009)" from the Open Library record. When you give a doi or an isbn, the authors and the year come from the record, and any authors or year you also pass are ignored.

With form "narrative" the author goes in your sentence and the rest stays in brackets, for a sentence like "Smith and Jones (2020, p. 14) argue that ...". With page "14", style "apa7" returns "Smith and Jones (2020, p. 14)", style "mla9" returns "Smith and Jones (14)" and style "chicago-ad" returns "Smith and Jones (2020, 14)". Three or more authors become "et al." in the narrative form too. With no authors given, the tool returns the parenthetical form.

## Prompts

### cite_this
Start a citation in APA 7, MLA 9 or Chicago author date from a DOI, an ISBN or details you type. The title names the default style, APA 7, and the style argument picks another one. The prompt returns the wording the citation tools use, so you can edit the source and send it. Arguments: style (apa7, mla9 or chicago-ad) and source (the DOI, the ISBN or the details), both optional. Example prompt: "Cite this journal article in APA 7: Learning to learn by John Kenneth Smith and Alice Jones, 2020, Journal of Study Skills, volume 4, issue 2, pages 11-25."

Parameters:
- style (optional): Citation style: apa7, mla9 or chicago-ad. Aliases such as APA, MLA 9 and Chicago are accepted. Defaults to apa7 when you leave it out or leave it blank.
- source (optional): The source to cite: a DOI, an ISBN, or the details of the source. Leave it out or leave it blank and write them in the message instead.

Example: with no arguments, returns one user message that starts with "Cite this source in APA 7.", names the tool that fits the source and lists the four example prompts, one for each tool. With source "10.1038/nature14539" it adds "Source: 10.1038/nature14539" and the line "That looks like a DOI, so use cite_from_doi.".

## Compared with the Zotero MCP servers
- zotero-mcp, @oscardvs/zoteus and @xbghc/zotero-mcp work with a Zotero library. Two of them talk to the Zotero desktop app and the third goes through the Zotero web API, so they need Zotero installed or an account at zotero.org.
- They search your library, read your PDFs, give you a passage with its page number and write notes and tags back into it. This server handles one source at a time and never writes.
- This server needs no account and no key, and formats APA 7, MLA 9 and Chicago author date.
